title: Categorical trace identity for a realized finite-stage Weil complex
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, with $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $F$ act on $C_c=R\Gamma_c(Y,K_E)$ by global geometric Frobenius [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. For $n\ge1$, let $P_n=Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$. For every $x\in P_n$ choose a $k$-point $\bar x:s\to Y$ obtained from $x$ through any $k_0$-embedding $\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$ and let $C_x=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}K_E)$ with local operator $f_{x,n}=F_x^{(n)}$ [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

Use the specified realization $(K_\Omega,\phi_\Omega)$ for the model Frobenius $\Phi$ and the specified compact-support and fixed-stalk comparisons of [lem-zl-general-condensed-weil-realization]. Put $\mathcal D_s=D^b_c(s)[[\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)]]$ and let $U_s$ be its coefficient unit. Write $P_c=Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K_\Omega$ and $P_x=L\bar x^*K_\Omega$. Let $G_n$ and $v_{x,n}$ be exactly its globalOperator and stalkFrobenius for the $n$-th iterated Weil map [nt-assume-trace-formula]. Let $\rho_{E,s}$ be the finite-matrix point realization of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace].

The set $P_n$ is finite and, through the fixed inclusion $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$, bijects with the model-Frobenius fixed $k$-points (the independently chosen lifts need not give this bijection); $C_c$ and the $C_x$ belong to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$. The objects $P_c$ and $P_x$ have right duals. The specified comparison isomorphisms $w_c:P_c\simeq\rho_{E,s}(C_c)$ and $w_x:P_x\simeq\rho_{E,s}(C_x)$ satisfy
$$w_cG_n=\rho_{E,s}(F^n)w_c,\qquad w_xv_{x,n}=\rho_{E,s}(f_{x,n})w_x.$$
For every such choice of the geometric points, the categorical traces [sk-d-trace] satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(G_n)=\sum_{x\in P_n}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(v_{x,n})\quad\text{in }\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal D_s}(U_s).$$

proof.text: By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $Y\to s$ is separated and of finite type, hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact. The projection $Y\to Y_0$ gives the required cartesian square. The $k$-linear endomorphism $\Phi=\Phi_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] is exactly a model Frobenius: on $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ it sends $a\otimes b$ to $a^q\otimes b$. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], the fixed scheme of $\Phi^n$ is the finite disjoint union of $s$ indexed by $P_n$. A $k$-point of that union selects exactly one summand, since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is connected, and its map to that summand is the identity over $s$. Thus scalar extension through the fixed inclusion gives a bijection $b_n:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\{z\in Y(k):\Phi^nz=z\}$. Write $z_x^0=b_n(x)$.

proof.text: By [prop-cohomological-finiteness], the cohomology of $C_c=R\Gamma_c(Y,K_E)$ is finite-dimensional over $E$ and zero outside a finite interval. For every geometric point, [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] places $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}K_E)$ in the same class. These are precisely the objects of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ by [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. Apply [lem-zl-general-condensed-weil-realization] to this datum, with the specified realization and its actual comparisons, rather than choosing new operators. Its intertwining assertion gives exactly $w_cG_n=\rho_{E,s}(F^n)w_c$ and $w_xv_{x,n}=\rho_{E,s}(f_{x,n})w_x$, for the same chosen lift on both sides. By [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace], every object isomorphic to the finite-matrix realization of such an $E$-complex has a right dual in $\mathcal D_s$. This supplies the right duals of $P_c$ and of every displayed $P_x$, including the canonical lifts $z_x^0$.

proof.text: We also check the stronger all-stalk hypothesis in [nt-assume-trace-formula]. Let $z:s\to Y$ be any $k$-point, and let $y\in Y_0$ be its image under projection. The residue-field map of [def-weil-residue-field] embeds $\kappa(y)$ into $k$, so it is algebraic over $k_0$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $\kappa(y)/k_0$ is finite; let its degree be $d\geq1$. A basis gives $|\kappa(y)|=q^d$, by the bijection between its elements and $d$-tuples of coefficients in $k_0$. By [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card], every element of its image in $k$ satisfies $u^{q^d}=u$. On an affine neighbourhood of $y$, the point evaluation factors through this residue field, so the affine formula of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] gives $\Phi^dz=z$. Hence $z$ is one of the fixed lifts indexed by $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^d})$ in [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]. Applying the comparison/right-dual clause of [lem-zl-general-condensed-weil-realization] at this degree $d$ gives a right dual of $Lz^*K_\Omega$. The carrier $K_\Omega$ of the specified realization is the same for all degrees; $d$ is used only to access its comparison. This proves existence of right duals at all rational points, with no uniform period required.

proof.text:
Apply [nt-assume-trace-formula] to the specified condensed Weil pair $(K_\Omega,\phi_\Omega)$ and $m=n\geq1$. Step 1 supplies its finite model and the finite fixed-point set. Steps 2–3 supply the global right dual and the right dual of every rational stalk, as the assumption requires. The finite-field datum supplies algebraic closedness of $k$ and $p\ne\ell$. Its operators are, by our definitions, precisely $G_n$ and the actual stalkFrobenius $S_{z,n}$ at a fixed $z$. Reindex its finite sum by the bijection $b_n$ of Step 1. This yields
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(G_n)=\sum_{x\in P_n}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(S_{z_x^0,n}).$$

proof.text: Fix $x\in P_n$ and its chosen embedding $e:\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$. By [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure], its image is the fixed subfield $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$. Relative to the inclusion, $e$ is an automorphism of this finite field. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], it is $u\mapsto u^{q^j}$ for some $j\geq0$. In an affine neighbourhood of the image of $x$, write $h_x:A_0\to\mathbf F_{q^n}$ for its point map. The canonical lift evaluates $a\otimes b$ as $h_x(a)b$. The chosen lift evaluates it as $e(h_x(a))b=h_x(a)^{q^j}b=h_x(a^{q^j})b$. The last expression is exactly the evaluation of $\Phi^jz_x^0$, by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Therefore $\bar x=\Phi^jz_x^0$ as $k$-points. All translates are $\Phi^n$-fixed since $\Phi^n$ commutes with $\Phi$, so each stalk operator used next is defined. This identifies the chosen point on its orbit; it does not assert that independently chosen points give a permutation of all fixed points.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-zl-condensed-stalk-frobenius-orbit-trace] to $(K_\Omega,\phi_\Omega)$, $m=n$ and successively to $z_x^0,\Phi z_x^0,\ldots,\Phi^{j-1}z_x^0$. Step 3 supplies the right duals at all these points. The base case $j=0$ is equality with itself; if the traces agree up to the $i$-th translate, the cited one-step equality equates the $(i+1)$-st trace to the $i$-th, completing induction. Thus
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(v_{x,n})=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(S_{z_x^0,n}).$$
Here $v_{x,n}=S_{\bar x,n}$ is the actual local operator, as fixed in the statement. Substitute this equality separately for each $x$ in the finite sum of Step 4. The result is the asserted categorical trace identity for every independent selection of lifts. No reindexing by that selection, and no passage from categorical to ordinary traces, is used. For $P_n=\varnothing$, Step 4 already gives trace zero and the substitution has no terms.

One new statement-only condensed orbit-invariance lemma, with an exact live project declaration attachment candidate. Clarified that the canonical bijection uses the fixed field inclusion, while arbitrary independent choices need not be bijective.
split_report.blueprint: Expands the trace-identity sentence in prop-every-iterate-trace.proof.md: steps 1–3 verify its fixed-point, realization and duality inputs, step 4 applies the categorical assumption, and steps 5–6 justify arbitrary choices of geometric lifts.

tool_uses.why: Finite-dimensional bounded compact cohomology, used before invoking the categorical assumption; that assumption requires rather than proves duality.
Only its right-dual transport to objects isomorphic to finite-matrix point realizations is used; no trace conversion is needed.
Coefficient and operator comparison without a trace identity; fixes the realization used in the item.
Geometric identification and finiteness of the model-Frobenius fixed k-points; not supplied by the cited trace assumption.
Finite residue fields of points of a finite-type scheme whose residue field embeds in the algebraic closure of the finite base; used only for periodicity of arbitrary k-points.
Finite-field power identity, used to check periodicity of every rational stalk, not a trace theorem.
Batch-5 categorical trace assumption is the sole source of the global trace identity; all its hypotheses are checked in steps 1–3.

(1) Statement change: 'geometric point over x' became 'k-point from any k_0-embedding'. This is the realization lemma's own meaning, so it is not a narrowing. The citer prop-every-iterate-trace still gets its 'every selection' clause and its comparisons. The report's collision example on A^1 at n=2 is correct. (2) Steps 1–6 hold. Fix(Φ^n) is a coproduct of Spec k over P_n by thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points. Duals come from point-supertrace via the realization comparisons. Every k-point z is Φ^d-fixed with d=[κ(y):k_0] (residue-field embedding, kun-closed-point-field(a), pow-card), which gives the all-stalk duals the assumption needs. I checked every hypothesis of nt-assume-trace-formula and found it satisfied. The chosen lift equals Φ^j z^0: I recomputed this on A_0⊗k using unique-subfield and Gal=⟨x^q⟩. The induction through the new node is explicit, and the termwise substitution survives lift collisions. (3) The new node is true: it is conjugation by Lz^*ψ plus trace invariance. It is exactly the live Lean Stalk.lean:238–250 trace_stalkFrobenius_comp (sorry-free; context: field k with characteristic prime ≠ ℓ, X locally of finite type, quasi-compact and separated). It is statement-only, self-contained, smaller than the item, and does not duplicate lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy (finite coefficients), lem-weil-local-frobenius-conjugacy-class, prop-trf-trace-formal-laws or any other stalkFrobenius node.
